<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e58e0a27998194640c145344b7519f1ccc9fad4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `57b6c06cdf356dcb0fab67aeec303dbcf5a8494a` — the merge of head `69f76c6ef1a3e64bd6c7d1c8faaea31f84d3686b` into base `7e58e0a27998194640c145344b7519f1ccc9fad4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 57b6c06cdf356dcb0fab67aeec303dbcf5a8494a && git checkout 57b6c06cdf356dcb0fab67aeec303dbcf5a8494a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7e58e0a27998194640c145344b7519f1ccc9fad4 69f76c6ef1a3e64bd6c7d1c8faaea31f84d3686b && git checkout -B drift-repro 7e58e0a27998194640c145344b7519f1ccc9fad4 && git merge --no-ff 69f76c6ef1a3e64bd6c7d1c8faaea31f84d3686b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e58e0a27998194640c145344b7519f1ccc9fad4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `69f76c6ef1a3e64bd6c7d1c8faaea31f84d3686b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/24468-lint-rule-hop-undeclared-field.md, .changeset/24468-objectql-rule-hop-sibling-isolation.md, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.rule-one-hop.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.object-validation-writes.test.ts, (`readClause2Line`), scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs (`--paths`, the face), .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (`Check Changeset`) and .github/workflows/ci.yml (the two speeds), packages/platform-objects, packages/plugins, packages/services, packages/runtime, non-test ts/yml/yaml/json)

Inputs: card #24468 (body; triage 6260730682, claim 6262728643, dispatch 6262791718, the dev's os-dev-report 6263711750, all read as claims; the `domain:spec` declarations 6262742638 on #6017 and 6262753494 on #18549), the landed formula twin #24410 (body) and PR #24466 (`45bec43cd9`; body; records 6260609012 FAIL and 6262025060 PASS, the pattern this diff follows), PR #24508 (body, the 12-file list, the 6 commits), the net diff `959ee317b1..69f76c6ef1` (merge base `959ee317b1`, the dev's pre-PR merge of `origin/main`; +514/−12 over 12 files, agreeing with the PR's file list and the report's line budget; fetched into `refs/remotes/pr/24508` and read with `git diff`, `git show` and `git grep`; nothing checked out, built, run or re-run), and the head's check-runs.

Check-runs on the head, four reads. First (about 09:10Z): 38 runs, 17 success, 6 skipped, 15 in progress. Second (09:18:53Z) and third (09:21:49Z): 40 runs, 28 success, 6 skipped, the six `Test Core` shards in progress. Final (09:28:29Z): 40 runs, 32 success, 6 skipped by design (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the three Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), **2 still in progress: `Test Core (2/6)` and `Test Core (4/6)`** (started 09:08:16Z); `Test Core (1/6)`, `(3/6)`, `(5/6)` and `(6/6)` concluded success (09:23–09:27Z); the aggregate `Test Core` has not yet appeared. **No run has concluded failure.** Green at the final read, among them: `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, every Lint job (CI/release/engine gates, ESLint, repo & tooling gates, docs & code guards, PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped jobs), Type Check source/consumer/debt/workspace, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate (its three shards skipped on a `pull_request` run: ci.yml's two speeds), Flag docs affected by code changes, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, and the three claim and card guards. The runs were taken on the merge of `69f76c6ef` into the PR's base `7e58e0a27` (the docs-drift comment names `57b6c06cdf` as that merge), so the one `main` commit the dev did not merge is inside what they measured.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The refusal, as implemented** — RIGHT. `refuseUndeclaredHopField` (validate-expressions.ts 1998–2027 at the head) takes a `site` and is now called from `check()` (2209) under `objectName && traversalHydration`, right after `refuseStoredMetadataBodyHop`, and from `judgeFieldFormula` (2932) with `'formula'`. `check()` receives `traversalHydration` at exactly two call sites: a rule's top-level `condition` (2793, `true`) and a nested predicate whose `slot === 'condition'` (2812) — a `script` / `cross_field` rule's `condition` inside a `conditional`'s `then` / `otherwise` at any depth (`rulePredicates`, 559–581). A `when`, top-level (2798) or nested (2812 with slot `when`), passes no hydration and is not judged. That set is the engine's hydration set exactly: `collectPredicateRelationships` (rule-validator.ts 548–570) collects `script` / `cross_field` conditions, recursing into `conditional.then` / `otherwise` and never into `when`; `evaluateRule` (3745–3760) hands `ctx.related` to `checkPredicate` for `script` / `cross_field` only; `state_machine`, `format` and `json_schema` take no hop; `checkConditional` (4653–4674) evaluates `when` on `ruleScope(ctx.merged, ctx.previous)`, unhydrated. No rule type other than `script` / `cross_field` hydrates, and the lint judges those two and nothing else. The per-column verdict: `column === 'id' || fieldIndex.get(target)?.includes(column)` admits; a target `fieldIndex` has no entry for, or in the stored-metadata-body family, is skipped; the issue lands in the rule pass's `issues` under the existing `expression-invalid` rule — no new code, as the door pin (`expressionFindings(result.errors)`) and the booted pin (`issues[].rule === 'expression-invalid'`) assert. The message opens with the shared validator's "unknown field `COLUMN` on `TARGET`" words, names the read (`record.account`), the target, the per-site consequence ("so the rule has no verdict and every write it judges is refused") and where not to declare it. One body serves `os validate`, `os build` and the door: the rule loop is "NOT fenced on an object write" (2781–2783) and the door's `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` runs the same pass (precedent 6260609012 ①.3, unchanged code).

2. **"Declared" is exactly declared fields + injected system columns + `id`** — RIGHT, and it coincides with the loader's set. `fieldIndex` is `buildFieldIndex(objects)` (170–200): the authored field names, in either `fields` shape, union `injectedColumnsFor(obj)` = `resolveInjectedSystemColumns(obj).names` (system-fields.ts 74–75; injected-system-columns.ts 186–240: `organization_id` per tenancy, the audit provenance family, `owner_id` / `owning_business_unit_id` by ownership tier, no ownership anchors on `sys_*` or `managedBy` objects), plus `id` at the call (2018). The engine's "declared" on the predicate seam is `this._registry.getObject(target).fields` plus `id` (`undeclaredRelatedFields`, engine.ts 2677–2683), and the registry's field map carries the injected columns (`applySystemFields`, as 6260609012 ①.1 read it on the same code). So the door refuses exactly the rules whose hop column the loader answers `undeclared-field` — the rules that have no verdict and refuse every write today.

3. **Can a rule that WORKS today be refused?** Judged per case:
   - an injected column on the target (`record.account.created_at`, `record.account.owner_id`): admitted — `created_at` pinned (rule-one-hop pin), the rest derived from the plan the registry itself injects. A bare `record.account.owner` is refused: `owner` is no injected column name (`OWNER_COLUMN` is `owner_id`), and the engine's `'owner' in declared` refuses it today too — nothing working is lost. On a platform-global target `organization_id` stays admitted (the lint derives without `platformGlobalObjects`): a missed catch, never a refusal;
   - a field an `extend` contributor or an `objectExtensions` body adds to the target: **at the door, admitted.** The door's `context.objects` is `listCollection('object', 'objects')` over the live registry (protocol.ts 7414), whose `getAllObjects` → `resolveObject(fqn)` → `foldExtenders` (registry.ts 3413, 3426, 4369, 4387) is the merged object; `buildRuntimeWriteSnapshots` narrows that list (runtime-gate.ts 706–709) without unfolding. At `os build` / `os validate` the stack's authored objects are the index, so such a rule is refused at build although it evaluates at runtime — the same window the formula site has, stated in the lint changeset's "What to do" and carried from 6262025060 ②/③.5;
   - a target declared in another package of the closure: judged at the door (limb 4 of `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure`, 415–437, `packageScope.dependencies`) — pinned, `fx_account` from `com.example.accounts` beside its valid sibling, the LIT naming exactly one finding; at build, judged when the stack carries it;
   - a system-object target: carried at the door unconditionally (limb 1, `isSystemObject`); a `user` field's implicit `sys_user` is judged against `sys_user`'s declared fields;
   - a target the snapshot does not carry: not judged (`fieldIndex.has(target)` false) — pinned (`hop_elsewhere`). A missed catch, never a false refusal;
   - case or label forms of a column (`Status`, `Account Status`): refused, exactly as the loader's `n in declared` refuses them at runtime — nothing working is lost;
   - a non-CEL dialect condition (`js`): `celSourceOf` (532–541) answers undefined, so it is not judged; the engine's `celSourceOfSlot` collects no hop from it either. Consistent;
   - a read more than one hop deep (`record.account.owner.email`): not judged here (`analysis.multiHopFields.has(field)`), refused by the traversal arm's `multi-hop` verdict — refused either way;
   - a `conditional`'s `when` through a lookup: not judged (no hydration flag), and it faults at runtime — ③.10.
   Net: the save door newly refuses exactly the `script` / `cross_field` conditions whose one-hop column the predicate loader marks undeclared, each of which refuses every write today. No rule that evaluates on a real row is refused.

4. **Other predicate surfaces through the same hop.** A field's `requiredWhen` / `readonlyWhen` / `conditionalRequired` and an option's `visibleWhen` that read through a reference are already refused WHOLE under `expression-invalid` by the field-level traversal refusal (`fieldTraversalMessage`, 1264–1295: "a field-level predicate never reads the related record ... faults on every row", prescribing a `validations[]` `script` rule); the CLI pin (`validate-field-predicate-traversal.test.ts` 168–185) shows the three slots refused and the same traversal in `validations[]` clean. Nothing hydrates there (`collectPredicateRelationships`' docblock: "the field level is not hydrated at all"), so this pass neither reaches them nor needs to. A `conditional`'s `when`: `checkConditional` evaluates it unhydrated and the lint opts it out of the traversal checks (2795–2799) and, carrying no hydration flag, out of this check — the #22042 pin's `topWhen` case shows `record.account.owner.email` in a `when` saving with no finding. The dev's reading is right; the filing-gate question is answered in ③.10.

5. **The multi-hop skip at the FORMULA site** — RIGHT, and no formula verdict moves. `multiHopFields` holds the first field of a `record.a.b.c` read (`traversalsOf`, relationship-traversal.ts 248–264). At the formula site `judgeFieldFormula` runs `validateExpression('value', …, traversalHydration: true, fieldTypes)` whose traversal arm (validate.ts 1131–1137 → `findFormulaTraversalConflicts`, relationship-traversal.ts 426–436) refuses every multi-hop read through a `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` field — the same type set `referenceTargetOf` resolves a target for — so every field this check would have judged is already refused there. Before this diff, a multi-hop formula whose FIRST leaf was undeclared on the target earned two findings (the `multi-hop` refusal and "unknown field LEAF"); after it, one. A multi-hop formula whose first leaf is declared — the formula-one-hop pin's `record.book.shelf.code`, `shelf` declared on `hop_book` — earned one before and one after, which is why that pin's `toHaveLength(1)` always held. No accept changes, no refusal changes; only a second finding on an already-refused expression goes away. **The formula message is byte-identical:** the `'formula'` arm of `undeclaredHopFieldMessage` (1783–1796) reassembles the previous string exactly ("…, and 'T' declares no field 'X', so the formula reads null on every row. Read a field 'T' declares, or declare 'X' on 'T' — not on 'O', the object carrying this formula."), and the unchanged formula-one-hop and object-formula-writes pins assert its opening and its prescription.

6. **The isolation** — RIGHT, proven by the diff. `resolvePredicateRelated` (engine.ts 10207–10281): `wanted` is built fresh per call (`collectPredicateRelationships` allocates `out` anew, so the deletions mutate no shared state); per reference with a target — a stored-metadata-body target is left to the loader's own `unreadable` verdict — the registry target's `fields` are read and `undeclaredRelatedFields` splits the union; the missing columns are deleted from the shared set and recorded per reference; a reference left with nothing is dropped; the loader is called with the declared rest under `'predicate'`. **`resolveOneHopRelated` (10314–10500) has no hunk in this PR**, so the record-access semantics stand byte for byte: `bound = authority === 'predicate' && !caller?.isSystem`, `readsNothing` under the wall, the caller's own read on a federated or tenant-less target, the #22892 master-detail header door, the system-context read projecting `['id', ...named]` and nothing more. Nothing undeclared enters the system read — before, the whole reference was skipped; now the declared subset is read, which is the read the valid rule gets alone. The wrapper spreads `undeclaredFields` onto each affected reference's binding and, where no declared column remained, binds `{ object, unavailable: 'undeclared-field' }` so no rule meets a bare id. `resolveTraversalScope` (rule-validator.ts 4167–4232): after the shape conflicts, the new block intersects THIS rule's named columns with `binding.undeclaredFields` and refuses through `traversalRefusal('undeclared-field', own)` — summary "'T' declares no 'region'", naming only its own; a rule naming none proceeds to (2)/(3) and hydrates `binding.row` (or meets `no-reference` / `unresolved` / `unreadable`) exactly as it does alone; no binding at all keeps the pre-#18682 bare-id path. Pinned: the valid sibling admits and refuses as alone; the bad rule names only `not_a_column`; one system read projecting `['id', 'type']`; two undeclared names on one binding and the bad rule names only its own; a fully undeclared reference still refuses. The inference channel the loader's docblock accepts does not widen: a sibling's verdict is now exactly its alone-verdict, so nothing is disclosed beyond the alone case. **The formula seam does not move:** `resolveFormulaRelated` (6287–6333), `formulaHopScope` (2713–2746), `formulaHopRefusal` and `applyFormulaPlan` have no hunk.

7. **The census rows.** objectql `federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts` keys `file#function :: seam()`; its `SEAM_CALLS` (112–121) name `referenceTargetOf` and not `isStoredMetadataBodyObject` or `getObject`, so the new call inside `resolvePredicateRelated` is one new key and the one row added is the one owed. `caller-predicate` is not an ASKS disposition (those are `skips` / `exempt` / `excludes`), so its `why` is the reviewer's claim to check — "judges a validation rule's own hop against the target's declared field map; no row is read here" is true: the block reads the registry's field map and no row (rows are read in `resolveOneHopRelated`, whose own `exempt` rows stand). It is the class of its sibling `resolveFormulaRelated` row. `packages/core`'s `[#22661]` census is **per file**: `CALLERS` is keyed by path (pin 127–245) and assertion (i) requires every non-test `.ts` under `packages/` with a code-line call of `referenceTargetOf` to have a row. This diff adds calls only in `engine.ts` (row `executes`, whose `also` prose already names `resolvePredicateRelated`) and `validate-expressions.ts` (row `not-a-served-read`, #24410); `rule-validator.ts`'s `isReference` call pre-exists with its row. No new caller FILE, no new row owed — the dev's reading holds.

8. **The pins** — RIGHT and sufficient for the two halves. Lint: the refusal naming field and target; `id` and `created_at` admitted; an absent target not judged; the door with a cross-package target beside its valid sibling, a nested `then`, and the control. Objectql: the engine sibling served as alone both ways with one read, the validator's per-rule verdicts. Booted: 422 `INVALID_METADATA` with one `expression-invalid` issue at `validation 'north_only'`; the control saves 200; the valid rule alone 201 / 400; the stored copy judged per rule on open and closed accounts. No title states a value. The dogfood pin is selected by the `isolated` project's glob (vitest.config.ts: every test file minus `SHARED_SHOWCASE`), so it is not silently excluded — but on a `pull_request` run the three dogfood shards are skipped by design, so its 4/4 at this head is the dev's claim, re-measured by `main`'s full battery after landing (③.13.d).

9. **Public surface and corpus.** No export moves in either package; `undeclaredHopFieldMessage` and `refuseUndeclaredHopField` are closure-local; `RelatedFieldBinding.undeclaredFields` already existed, optional, and the interface is not re-exported from objectql's index. The card's two targets are met at this head. In-tree, exactly one shipped rule condition reads through a lookup: `examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/invoice.object.ts:191`, `record.account.status == 'churned'`, where `account` is a lookup to `showcase_account` (invoice.object.ts:73) and `showcase_account` declares `status` (account.object.ts:69) — admitted. No other `condition` line in examples, platform-objects, plugins, services, runtime or the scaffolding templates (non-test ts/yml/yaml/json) reads `record.X.Y`. The sibling test fixtures that traverse — cli `trav_account.tier`, plugin-security `qa_line.kind`, `os_ehr_line.kind`, `crm_account.type` — declare the column or carry one rule per reference, so neither half moves their verdicts.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/lint` `minor` with `fix(lint)!:`, `**BREAKING**`, the launch-window sentence, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at the start of a line, the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` comment marker, a FROM → TO, a "What to do" and the `objectExtensions` sentence — RIGHT. An accept-set narrowing is breaking; the convention (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, "we ship breaking changes as `minor`" until GA) ships it `minor`. `breakingDeclaration` (check-adr-0087-registration.mjs 673–685) collects three signals (the banner, the `!`, the `narrowing` arm) and judges the file; exactly one marker is present; `no-migration-prescription` is in `CATEGORIES` (536–539) and is refused only when the body carries a framed consumer-code rewrite — the FROM → TO bullet here states the verdict change, not a rewrite — and the `Check Changeset` run (pr-automation.yml 244, the gate run with `--base`) is green, so the marker passed its re-validation. The reason is true: no spec key, stored shape or spelling moves; a stored rule with the fault stays stored and refuses as before; the only repair is the author's choice of column, which no `migrate meta` step can make.
- `@objectstack/objectql` `patch` with `Clause-②: no`, no arm and no marker — RIGHT, and rightly declared. `readClause2Line` reads `no` with `arm: null`; `breakingDeclaration` collects no signal (`patch`, no banner, `fix(objectql):` without a bang, no `narrowing` arm), which is the gate's G1 ("a non-breaking changeset is not this gate's business"), so no marker is owed — the correction 6260609012 ② asked of #24466, applied here from the start, and tidier than #24466's surplus marker (6262025060 ③.6.a). The code is a verdict fix only: nothing accepted is refused; a write wrongly refused on a sibling's fault is judged; the bad rule's refusal names its own columns; the predicate read keeps its authority and bound; no export moves.
- The PR body's third line begins `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — the fixed spelling at the start of a line, with the parenthetical rationale after it in the form #24466's body carried and 6262025060 ② read as right. `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` on the 12 paths says the paths decide no face and the lint changeset's `Clause-②` arm decides: `(narrowing)`, so the narrowing face and `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The `Served-tier` above is that reading.
- Corpus: ①.9 — one in-tree rule traverses a lookup and reads a declared column; zero shipped examples, packages, seeds or fixtures are refused.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Six pushes instead of one** (deviation 1). Process, no contract effect. AGENTS.md's "push a WIP commit before every step that takes minutes" is the standing rule and was followed; the "one push" is the round's prompt, not a rule I find in AGENTS.md or `.claude/**`, and reconciling the two is the dispatching seat's. All six are fast-forwards on the dev's own `claude/issue-*` branch; the net diff is what this record read.

2. **`validate-expressions.test.ts` beyond the claim's file surface** (deviation 2). Answered, right: the #5017 receiver census is a same-file meta-test that reds on any new local receiver in the rule code; `analysis` reads `traversals` and `multiHopFields`, the formula package's own result keys and never metadata keys, and the PLUMBING entry says so beside the #24316 `traversals` entry it extends. Same package, same lane, same pass family as the declared file, and inside the `domain:spec` declarations' "its pins beside it" (6262742638, 6262753494). Not a block.
